free_tier.stated: Bounded by the size of the git repo it builds from, not by a storage quota: a build fails with 'Git error. Max repo size 250MB exceeded'. JitPack builds any public git repo on demand and serves the resulting Maven artifacts at com.github.<user>.<repo>:<tag>.

egress.terms: Free. Artifacts served from jitpack.io CDN with no billing.

tooling: Any Maven/Gradle resolver pointed at https://jitpack.io; JitPack build API at /api/builds/<group>/<artifact> (open, returns build status per tag). No dedicated CLI beyond Maven/Gradle; no rclone backend.
chaining: unlimited public git repos x unlimited tags/commits x 250 MB repo each. Because artifacts are *derived*, storage is the repo's, and the same content is rebuilt per tag - so it amplifies, it does not multiply storage. 250 MB x N repos is the honest ceiling.
limits_note: per-object-cap: 250 MB repo size (hard build error). request-rate: builds are queued per-IP (anonymous builds are rate limited; the API exposes per-tag build state). retention: build artifacts are cached but a failing/expired build is rebuilt on demand - not durable storage.
reliability_note: Build service, not storage: artifacts can be evicted and rebuilt, and repo size is hard-capped at 250 MB. Read path live and public (verified /api/builds/com.github.jitpack/maven-simple returning ok states across dozens of tags).

evidence.proved: 'Build issue Max repo size 250MB exceeded'; 'Git error. Max repo size 250MB exceeded'
probe: GET -> 200 JSON, dozens of tag/commit entries with status 'ok'
